Diolch Rhian,

I'm currently at the Welsh Settlement in South Argentina, otherwise I'd be
there myself. So for our private study and research of our family land,
former home and history, we require photos be permitted to be taken, of
artifacts of interest, so they may be sent to me here.

I'm attempting to reconstruct a replica of our old 800 year old farm house
here as a museum/ open house. We're also trying to understand the
unresolved and ongoing ownership dispute between our family and BP, who
were awarded possession of our farm and home since 1667, which resulted in
us being dispossessed of our ancestral birthland as children in 1988. It's
all a very bizzar case.

The MP for Cardiff covering Llandough responded yesterday and is now aware
of the queries and concerns I'm raising with the case and we appreciate
your cooperation and service and thank you in advance. Subject to me
viewing the records, it's possible I may be warranted in proceeding with a
Senedd public enquiry request, as this could be a matter of public
interest.

No single centralised chronology with all supporting evidence appears to
exist for our land, family and former home and it's history and herritage.
And so this is the purposeful and meaningful work I have chosen to
undertake.

Fascinately world champion boxer Peerless Jim fought his first fight in our
barns. Marconi stayed with us while inventing radio. The house was a court
house and stood on a Roman villa and monestry. It's a trove of hidden
history.

Kind regards,

Requester

Dear BT Archives Team,

I am researching the General Post Office involvement in Guglielmo Marconi's South Wales wireless telegraphy experiments during 1897, particularly the experiments between Lavernock Point and Flat Holm.

The Postal Museum has advised that the relevant GPO Telegraph Department and Engineering Department records are likely to be held by BT Archives. They confirmed that their own searches of Postal Museum holdings found no relevant records and that surviving telecommunications material from this period is likely to be within the collections transferred to BT Archives.

I would be grateful if you could advise on the relevant surviving records and catalogue references.

My research concerns:

  *   Marconi's 1897 South Wales wireless experiments;
  *   Lavernock Point and Flat Holm;
  *   Penarth and Llandough (near Penarth);
  *   the involvement of the GPO Telegraph Department and Engineering Department;
  *   any surviving correspondence, reports, notebooks, engineering records, plans, photographs or administrative records connected with the experiments.

I am particularly interested in identifying any references to local residents or private individuals who assisted Marconi or GPO engineers. Family history suggests that a Mr Williams of Great House Farm, Llandough, may have assisted with the experiments locally. I appreciate that such a person may not appear in catalogue descriptions if he was a private individual rather than a GPO employee.

Could you please advise whether your catalogue contains references to any of the following terms or variants:

  *   Marconi
  *   Guglielmo Marconi
  *   wireless telegraphy
  *   South Wales experiments
  *   Lavernock
  *   Penarth
  *   Llandough
  *   Great House Farm
  *   Williams
  *   W. Williams
  *   William Williams
  *   Mr Williams

If relevant records exist, I would be grateful for the catalogue references, file descriptions and dates so that I can identify the material for further research.

I would also appreciate any guidance on whether there are related collections, transferred Post Office records, or finding aids that may not be obvious from the online catalogue.

Thank you very much for your assistance.

Kind regards,

Requester

Dear Mr Haste,

Thank you for your letter of *30 July 2026* concerning reference *N610CGV*
and the surviving records relating to the first registration of titles
*WA231076
and WA240304* at Great House Farm, Llandough.

I am writing to clarify the factual contents of the surviving
first-registration records and to identify the appropriate documents for
inspection/copying. *This is not a request to reopen my previous complaint,
nor am I asking HM Land Registry to determine the historical ownership
dispute.*

I would be grateful if you could clarify the following.
1. The 1971 Abstract of Title

You previously confirmed that a *1971 Abstract of Title* was seen in
connection with this matter.

Please confirm:

   - whether it still survives;
   - which title/file it relates to;
   - its item or document reference within the surviving records; and
   - whether it is available for inspection or copying.

2. The “question or doubt” certificate

Please confirm where in the surviving first-registration material the
certificate/declaration appears in which the applicant's solicitors stated
that they were *“not aware of any question or doubt affecting the title.”*

In particular, please confirm whether this forms part of the *Form 1E dated
30 November 1982*, or is a separate surviving document.
3. What the first-registration file records about other interests

Please confirm whether any of the surviving first-registration documents
contain any reference to:

   - *Mary Williams*;
   - *Fred Buckler*;
   - *William (Billy) Buckler*;
   - *Great House Farm / Ty Mawr* and its farmhouse, garden or curtilage;
   - any person other than the applicant asserting ownership or another
   interest in the land;
   - possession proceedings concerning the farmhouse or land; or
   - any objection, dispute, question or doubt concerning title.

I am asking this *solely as a factual question about the contents of the
surviving records*.

If no such reference appears in the surviving first-registration material,
confirmation of that fact would be sufficient.
4. Identification of the surviving documents

Your 30 July letter identifies, amongst other things, the *Form 1E, A13-DL
list of documents lodged and correspondence from Linklaters & Paines*.

Please identify the specific item numbers I should request by *Form OC2* to
obtain the fullest available surviving first-registration record,
particularly:

   - the title evidence submitted by the applicant;
   - the 1971 Abstract of Title, if it survives;
   - the A13-DL list of documents lodged;
   - correspondence with Linklaters & Paines;
   - examiner's notes, requisitions, memoranda or file notes, if any
   survive; and
   - any document recording the basis upon which the Registrar accepted the
   applicant's title.

If any of these categories do not survive, please identify which ones do
not.
5. Historic records relevant to identifying the land

I also wish to ensure that the correct physical parcel is being compared
with the land registered in 1982–83.

During recent research at the Glamorgan Archives, I have located historic
material concerning Great House Farm/Ty Mawr, including:

   - the *6 November 1877 Bute Estate counterpart lease to John Williams*;
   - the *1872 Llandough Rate Book*;
   - the *1924 and 1938 Great House Farm sale particulars and associated OS
   parcel references*; and
   - historic plans and notes concerning the farmhouse, gardens and
   associated boundaries.

These records appear potentially relevant to identifying the historic
extent and boundaries of the farmhouse and curtilage.

during the 1982/83 first-registration process identify the same physical
parcel and, if so, what documentary evidence was relied upon to establish
that identity.

contemporaneous document: *BP Properties Ltd's Certificate A dated 16
October 1989 in respect of outline application 89/01396/OUT*, in which BP

certification.

request.

July schedule which would provide the fullest surviving first-registration
record, I can request those documents directly.

to the *Form 1E, A13-DL list, title evidence, Linklaters & Paines
correspondence, the 1971 Abstract of Title, and any examiner/requisition
material that survives*.

Thank you for your assistance. I would be grateful for a substantive
clarification of the above points so that I can proceed with a properly
targeted inspection/copy request.

Regards,

*Requester*
*Sgt (Ret’d)*

  *   the Manor of Llandough (Glamorgan);

  *   pre-1667 references to occupants, customary tenants, holdings, surveys, rentals, terriers, or court rolls;

  *   Vaughan family estate holdings at Llandough;

  *   Great House Farm / Ty Mawr or any earlier description of the holding.

Any recorded information showing:

  *   whether records relating to Great House Farm, Llandough, the Bute Estate, Vaughan family papers, or associated land records were ever transferred to The National Archives;

  *   whether any such records were destroyed, and if so:

     *   what records were destroyed;

     *   when they were destroyed;

     *   under which retention schedule, disposal authority, or policy;

     *   which body authorised or carried out the destruction.

  *   Western Ground Rents Ltd;

  *   BP Pension Trust Ltd;

  *   BP Properties Ltd;

  *   Mountjoy Ltd;

  *   the proceedings connected with BP Properties Ltd v Buckler [1987] EWCA Civ 2.

  *   the Bute Estate;

  *   the 1938 sale or transfer of Great House Farm;

  *   Western Ground Rents Ltd acquisition;

  *   BP Pension Trust/BP Properties involvement;

  *   any government department involvement in the property.

Any correspondence, reports, enquiries, or administrative records held by The National Archives involving:

  *   Mary Williams;

  *   Fred Buckler;

  *   William Buckler;

  *   the Williams/Buckler family;

  *   Great House Farm / Ty Mawr;

  *   Bute Estate representatives;

  *   Western Ground Rents;

  *   BP entities.

  1.  1980–1988 period and demolition/eviction matters

Any records concerning:

  *   the public campaign regarding Great House Farm;

  *   parliamentary correspondence or government enquiries;

  *   the 1988 eviction/demolition;

  *   Cadw or government communications;

  *   European Commission of Human Rights Application 14464/88 (Buckler v United Kingdom).

If any relevant information is held, please provide catalogue references, descriptions, and access arrangements.

If no relevant information is held, please confirm:

  *   the searches undertaken;

  *   the catalogues, databases, and record series searched;

  *   whether any relevant records were ever held and subsequently transferred, destroyed, or disposed of.

BP Archive Team,

I am writing to enquire about records held within the BP corporate archive
relating to the former Great House Farm / Ty Mawr property at Llandough,
near Penarth, Glamorgan, South Wales.

I am conducting historical and legal research into the property, which was
acquired by BP Pension Trust Ltd in December 1969 and subsequently
administered by BP Properties Ltd. The property was the subject of
extensive litigation, including BP Properties Ltd v Buckler [1987] EWCA Civ
2, followed by the eviction of the occupying family in 1988 and demolition
of the farmhouse later that year.
Research context

The central issue of my research is the identification of the individual
parcels comprising the historic property.

The evidence currently being examined indicates that the historic complex
may have comprised separately identifiable:

   - a house-and-garden plot;
   - a western agricultural/farm plot containing the barn, stables and
   courtyard; and
   - an eastern cottages plot.

Later mapping and Land Registry records appear to have treated some of
these areas as a combined property.

I am therefore particularly interested in establishing *what BP itself
understood the boundaries and constituent parcels of the property to be*,
and when any change or consolidation of those parcels occurred.
Records sought

I would be grateful if the BP Archive could search its holdings for records
concerning:

   - BP Properties Ltd;
   - BP Pension Trust Ltd;
   - British Petroleum and relevant predecessor/subsidiary property records;
   - Great House Farm / Great House / Ty Mawr, Llandough;
   - Llandough-juxta-Penarth / Cogan / Penarth;
   - the Williams and Buckler families;
   - possession proceedings and enforcement, particularly 1955, 1962 and
   1974–1988;
   - property acquisition, title investigation and disposal;
   - conveyances, title deeds, abstracts of title and schedules of deeds;
   - estate-management correspondence;
   - property, site and boundary plans;
   - Land Registry correspondence and registration, particularly 1982–1983.

The relevant period is approximately *1955–1988*, with particular emphasis
on *1962–1983*.
Three priority categories

If relevant material survives, I would particularly like to identify the
following, in this order:

*1. The BP Properties Ltd / BP Pension Trust Ltd property file for Great
House Farm / Ty Mawr, Llandough*

In particular, any acquisition/title file containing the original property
description, conveyances, title investigation, schedules of deeds, property
plans, boundary plans or correspondence identifying exactly which land and
buildings BP considered to form the property.

*2. The legal/property file relating to the 1962 possession proceedings and
subsequent enforcement/re-entry*

In particular, any BP legal correspondence, instructions to solicitors,
plans, property descriptions or internal documents identifying the land and
buildings to which the possession order was understood to apply.

*3. The 1982–1983 title/registration/consolidation file*

In particular, correspondence, plans, conveyances, title investigation and
Land Registry material concerning the registration or amalgamation of the
relevant parcels, including any documentation showing how the
house-and-garden, eastern cottages and western farm/barn/stables/courtyard
areas were treated.

If these exact files do not survive, I would be very grateful for the
nearest surviving files, alternative references or catalogue entries
covering the same transactions.
Access

I would also appreciate advice on:

   - whether the relevant records are available for public research;
   - whether they can be viewed in person at the BP Archive at the
   University of Warwick;
   - whether advance appointment or reader registration is required;
   - whether particular records require advance retrieval;
   - whether copies or digital reproductions can be ordered; and
   - whether any relevant records are subject to closure or other access
   restrictions.

I am happy to provide further information, including the relevant court
case reference, property names, dates and Land Registry title numbers, if
this would assist the archivist in identifying the records.
Research purpose

I am particularly interested in *contemporary BP documentation rather than
later summaries*, because the central research question is what BP itself
understood the property's legal identity, boundaries and constituent
parcels to be at the relevant dates.

Thank you very much for any assistance you can provide.

Yours sincerely,

Requester

Thank you for your reply.

I understand that the BP Archive contains material up to the end of 1954,
but that post-1954 material is currently unavailable for external access.
My original enquiry did include the later BP acquisition, litigation and
registration records, so I understand that those parts of my request cannot
currently be accessed.

I would therefore like to clarify what *pre-1955 material concerning Great
House Farm / Ty Mawr* is held within the accessible BP Archive.

The reason this is particularly relevant is that Great House Farm was
subsequently acquired by *BP Pension Trust Ltd from Western Ground Rents in
1969*, and became the subject of *BP Properties Ltd v Buckler [1987] EWCA
Civ 2*. I am researching the underlying root of title and the history of
the family's occupation before *2 February 1955*, which is a critical date
in the subsequent dispute.

Could you please search the pre-1955 BP Archive holdings for Great House
Farm / Ty Mawr, Llandough, including references under:

   - Great House Farm / Great House / Ty Mawr
   - Llandough
   - Western Ground Rents Ltd
   - Mountjoy Ltd
   - Bute Estate / Llandough Estate
   - Williams
   - Buckler

In particular, I am looking for any surviving copies or references to:

   - the *1916 yearly tenancy agreement* between the Bute Estate and John
   Williams;
   - the *1924 Llandough Estate sale particulars — DSA/6/701*;
   - the *1938 Great House Farm auction particulars — GD/LA/15/255 and
   DSA/6/1158*;
   - the *1938 conveyance from Mountjoy Ltd to Western Ground Rents*;
   - the *1949 agreement or correspondence* concerning Frederick Buckler
   and Mary Williams taking over the occupation;
   - the *1953 judgment concerning rent arrears* at Great House Farm; and
   - any *notice to quit issued before 2 February 1955*.

I would also be interested in any pre-1955 *plans, title descriptions,
schedules of deeds, abstracts of title or other records* showing how the
farmhouse, garden, farmyard, cottages and agricultural land were described
or treated.

I appreciate that some of these documents may have originated with the Bute
Estate, Mountjoy or Western Ground Rents rather than BP itself. What I am
trying to establish is whether any such historical material is present
within the BP Archive, or whether the BP Archive has catalogue references
identifying material which may have subsequently formed part of the title
history of the property.

If the answer is that the BP Archive contains *no pre-1955 material
relating to Great House Farm / Ty Mawr*, I would be grateful if you could
confirm that explicitly. If you can identify relevant catalogue references
even where the underlying document is not held, those references would also
be very useful.

Thank you again for your assistance.

Regards,

Requester

Michelle,

Thanks for your prompt response.

I'd like to request an internal review of the handling of my enquiry and,
insofar as it constitutes a Freedom of Information request, of the
conclusion that no relevant records are held.

I am not challenging the conclusion simply because it is inconvenient to my
enquiry. Rather, I would like to establish whether an adequate search was
undertaken before the conclusion was reached.

Your latest response states that the Medical Examiner Service would not
hold “any records whatsoever” or have “any knowledge” of these patients.
Given that the deaths occurred in 1983 and 1990, before the establishment
of the current Medical Examiner Service, I would be grateful if the
internal review could specifically establish whether the search extended
beyond current Medical Examiner records to any relevant predecessor, legacy
or transferred records.

In particular, could the review please confirm:

   1.

   What records and information systems were searched;
   2.

   Whether any legacy or predecessor records relating to the medical
   examination or certification of deaths were considered;
   3.

   Whether records relating to Llandough Hospital, where William Buckler is
   recorded as having died in approximately May 1990, are held by the Medical
   Examiner Service, NHS Wales Shared Services Partnership, another NHS body,
   or an archive to which you have access or knowledge;
   4.

   Whether any records concerning referrals to a coroner, inquests,
   post-mortems or other investigations into these deaths would have been held
   separately from Medical Examiner records;
   5.

   Whether the possibility of records having been transferred to an archive
   or successor organisation was considered;
   6.

   Whether the statement that no records are held means that no relevant
   records are held by the South Wales Central Medical Examiner Service
   specifically, or that searches have established that no such records are
   held anywhere within NHS Wales Shared Services Partnership; and
   7.

   If the records are not held by your organisation, whether you can
   identify the appropriate current custodian or archive for any surviving
   historical records.

For clarity, the individuals concerned are:

   - William (Billy) Buckler – died at Llandough Hospital on or about 29
   May 1990, aged 41; and
   - Mary Doreen Williams – born 10 August 1913; death registered in March
   1983, South Glamorgan, Vol. 28, p. 3029.

I would be grateful if this could be treated as a formal internal review
rather than simply a further general enquiry.

I would also ask that the review be undertaken by someone who was not
responsible for the original response, where practicable.

My purpose is to establish a reliable documentary record and, in
particular, to distinguish between:

(a) records which do not exist;

(b) records which once existed but have been destroyed;

(c) records which exist but are held by another organisation; and

(d) records which are held within NHS Wales or a predecessor organisation
but were not identified by the original search.

I would be grateful for confirmation of the review and, where applicable,
the relevant FOI reference number.

Kind regards,

Requester

Bev,

Thank you for clarifying the position regarding the Freedom of Information
Act.

I understand that coroners and their records are not subject to the FOI
access regime. I am therefore not seeking to pursue the matter as an FOI
request if that is not the appropriate route.

My primary purpose is to establish whether either of these deaths was ever
referred to the coroner and, if so, whether any surviving record exists and
what lawful route is available for an interested family member to obtain
information from it.

I would therefore be grateful if you could clarify the following, insofar
as you are able:

   1.

   Whether your office has any record or index indicating that either
   William (Billy) Buckler, who died at Llandough Hospital on or about 29 May
   1990, or Mary Doreen Williams, whose death was registered in March 1983 in
   South Glamorgan (Vol. 28, p. 3029), was reported to or dealt with by the
   coroner;
   2.

   If either death was the subject of a coroner's investigation, whether an
   inquest, post-mortem examination or other coroner's investigation took
   place;
   3.

   Whether any historical record relating to either death remains in the
   custody of the coroner's service, or whether such records have been
   transferred to another archive, authority or successor body;
   4.

   If records exist but cannot be disclosed directly, what procedure is
   available for a descendant or other interested person to establish the
   basic factual information concerning the case;
   5.

   If your office has no record whatsoever of either death, whether that
   means that no coroner's record exists, or simply that the surviving records
   are no longer held by your office.

I am particularly interested in establishing the documentary chain rather
than necessarily seeking disclosure of confidential medical information. A
confirmation that a death was, or was not, referred to the coroner would
itself be useful.

If you are not the appropriate office to answer these historical-record
questions, I would be grateful if you could identify the relevant archive,
successor body or other custodian to whom I should direct the enquiry.

Thank you again for your assistance.

Regards,


Requester

Michelle,

Thanks for your prompt response.

I'd like to request an internal review of the handling of my enquiry and, insofar as it constitutes a Freedom of Information request, of the conclusion that no relevant records are held.

I am not challenging the conclusion simply because it is inconvenient to my enquiry. Rather, I would like to establish whether an adequate search was undertaken before the conclusion was reached.

Your latest response states that the Medical Examiner Service would not hold “any records whatsoever” or have “any knowledge” of these patients. Given that the deaths occurred in 1983 and 1990, before the establishment of the current Medical Examiner Service, I would be grateful if the internal review could specifically establish whether the search extended beyond current Medical Examiner records to any relevant predecessor, legacy or transferred records.

In particular, could the review please confirm:

  1.  What records and information systems were searched;

  2.  Whether any legacy or predecessor records relating to the medical examination or certification of deaths were considered;

  3.  Whether records relating to Llandough Hospital, where William Buckler is recorded as having died in approximately May 1990, are held by the Medical Examiner Service, NHS Wales Shared Services Partnership, another NHS body, or an archive to which you have access or knowledge;

  4.  Whether any records concerning referrals to a coroner, inquests, post-mortems or other investigations into these deaths would have been held separately from Medical Examiner records;

  5.  Whether the possibility of records having been transferred to an archive or successor organisation was considered;

  6.  Whether the statement that no records are held means that no relevant records are held by the South Wales Central Medical Examiner Service specifically, or that searches have established that no such records are held anywhere within NHS Wales Shared Services Partnership; and

  7.  If the records are not held by your organisation, whether you can identify the appropriate current custodian or archive for any surviving historical records.

For clarity, the individuals concerned are:

  *   William (Billy) Buckler – died at Llandough Hospital on or about 29 May 1990, aged 41; and
  *   Mary Doreen Williams – born 10 August 1913; death registered in March 1983, South Glamorgan, Vol. 28, p. 3029.

I would be grateful if this could be treated as a formal internal review rather than simply a further general enquiry.

I would also ask that the review be undertaken by someone who was not responsible for the original response, where practicable.

My purpose is to establish a reliable documentary record and, in particular, to distinguish between:

(a) records which do not exist;

(b) records which once existed but have been destroyed;

(c) records which exist but are held by another organisation; and

(d) records which are held within NHS Wales or a predecessor organisation but were not identified by the original search.

I would be grateful for confirmation of the review and, where applicable, the relevant FOI reference number.

Kind regards,

Requester

records.transcript:
Glamorgan Archives Team,

I am writing to make a targeted archive research enquiry concerning the
DBDT collection and any related Bute, Mountjoy or Western Ground Rents
material held by Glamorgan Archives.

I am investigating the historic title, occupation and parcel
boundaries of *Great
House Farm (Tŷ Mawr), Llandough*, particularly evidence concerning a
possible historical division of the farm between land retained by the Bute
Estate and land allegedly sold or transferred to *Daniel Thomas*.

A family witness account describes a specific arrangement under which
approximately ten acres, including the farmhouse, were allegedly sold by
the Bute Estate to Daniel Thomas, while a separate portion of approximately
nine acres remained under the Bute Estate. The account further describes
quarrying on the Thomas-held land and an agreement under which the freehold
would eventually pass to the occupying family when quarrying ceased.

I appreciate that this account requires verification against the original
documentary record. I am therefore seeking to identify the relevant deeds,
agreements, plans and subsequent title documents.
1. Verification of specific DBDT catalogue entries

Please confirm the exact property description, parties and date of the
following catalogue entries, and, if possible, provide a digital copy or
scan of the opening parties clause and any attached or marginal plan:

   -

   *DBDT10/19* – Lease (counterpart), described in the catalogue as
   concerning land and messuages in Bute Street, Cardiff, from trustees of the
   late Marquess of Bute to Mr Daniel Thomas, October 1850.
   -

   *DBDT10/20* – Agreement for a building lease of premises in Bute Town,
   Cardiff, involving the same parties, June 1849.

I understand from the catalogue descriptions that these items concern
Cardiff rather than Llandough. My purpose is to establish whether the *Daniel
Thomas named in these instruments can be identified sufficiently to
determine whether he is the same individual later connected with the
Llandough lime works and land interests*, or whether these are unrelated
transactions involving another person of the same name.

Please also advise whether either document contains information identifying
Daniel Thomas by residence, occupation, estate, trusteeship or other
distinguishing details.
2. Targeted search for a Bute–Daniel Thomas transaction at or near Llandough

Please search the catalogue descriptions and indexes available to Glamorgan
Archives for any deed, conveyance, exchange, sale, transfer, lease,
agreement, plan or related instrument involving:

   - *Daniel Thomas*;
   - *Alfred Thomas*;
   - the *Marquess of Bute*;
   - trustees of the Marquess of Bute;
   - the *Bute Estate*;

and land at or near:

   - *Llandough*;
   - *Great House Farm / Great House / Tŷ Mawr*;
   - adjoining land or parcels that may subsequently have formed part of
   the farm.

I am particularly interested in transactions dating from approximately *1876
to 1878*, but would be grateful for references to earlier or later
documents where they form part of the same chain of title.

In particular, I am seeking evidence capable of confirming or disproving
whether any defined parcel of land was conveyed by the Bute Estate to
Daniel Thomas.
3. Quarrying, lime works and any conditional reversion or transfer

Please identify any relevant records concerning land at Llandough or Great
House Farm that refer to:

   - quarrying;
   - quarries or quarry land;
   - lime works or lime kilns;
   - mineral rights;
   - removal of quarrying machinery;
   - reduction or cessation of rent as land was quarried;
   - termination of quarrying;
   - a future conveyance, reversion, surrender or transfer of a freehold
   interest when quarrying ceased.

The particular issue I am investigating is whether an agreement existed
under which occupation or ownership of a defined parcel was intended to
change when quarrying operations came to an end.
4. Daniel Thomas, Alfred Thomas and the Llandough lime works

Please identify any documents linking *Daniel Thomas*, or his son *Alfred
Thomas (later Lord Pontypridd)*, with:

   - land at Llandough;
   - the Llandough lime works or lime kilns;
   - quarrying operations;
   - Great House Farm or adjoining agricultural land;
   - any freehold or leasehold interest in the area.

I would be particularly interested in estate papers, correspondence,
conveyances, wills, probate-related estate records, rentals, rent books,
abstracts of title and plans that may trace what became of any Daniel
Thomas interest after his death or thereafter.
5. Subsequent title and occupation

Please identify any abstracts of title, estate maps, conveyances,
correspondence, tenancy records or other material that may assist in
establishing:

   1. what happened to any freehold interest held by Daniel Thomas or his
   estate;
   2. whether such an interest was ever conveyed, surrendered or
   transferred back to the Bute Estate or another party;
   3. whether the Bute Estate later reacquired any relevant parcel;
   4. whether later parties, including *Mountjoy Ltd* or *Western Ground
   Rents Ltd*, acquired title to land previously held by Daniel Thomas or
   his successors;
   5. the basis on which later tenancies described as covering the "whole"
   of Great House Farm were granted.

I am also interested in any material linking these title questions with the
occupation of the farm by the *Williams family*.
6. Plans and parcel boundaries

A separate line of research concerns the possibility that historic legal
boundaries passed through or between different parts of the Great House
Farm complex.

Accordingly, please identify any:

   - estate maps;
   - conveyance plans;
   - tenancy plans;
   - quarry plans;
   - large-scale plans;
   - boundary plans;
   - valuation plans;

that show Great House Farm, the farmhouse, garden, stables, outbuildings or
adjoining parcels.

I am particularly interested in documents that could establish whether
different parts of the historic building complex fell within different
legal parcels.

I appreciate that some of these requests may require staff research beyond
a standard enquiry. My immediate priority is to obtain *the relevant
catalogue references and confirmation of what material exists*. If more
detailed searching or document retrieval is necessary, please let me know
the applicable procedure, estimated cost and whether a formal paid research
request would be required.

If relevant documents have been digitised, I would be grateful for details
of the cost of obtaining copies. Otherwise, please advise whether they can
be consulted in person and whether any restrictions or advance ordering
requirements apply.

Thank you for your assistance. The documents identified through this
enquiry may be important to reconstructing the historical chain of title
and occupation of Great House Farm, Llandough from the nineteenth century
onwards.

Yours faithfully,

*Requester *
